Parses a wide range of input (git command output, grep results, search results, etc.) and shows a terminal UI to select which files you care about. You can then open them in your editor or run arbitrary commands on the selection.

Accepts output from git commands, grep results, searches — pretty much anything. After parsing, PathPicker presents a UI to select files, then you can open them in your favorite editor or execute arbitrary commands.
Besides opening files in an editor, you can run arbitrary commands with the selected files: add to version control, change permissions, scp, delete, etc.
A transfer of money from a payer to a payee to settle a purchase, a bill or a debt, made through a payment method such as a card, a bank transfer or a wallet.
Pay/ment/Manage/ment explains how software systems let people store and choose payment methods.
Payment management is a feature of software systems that lets a person store, choose, update and remove the payment methods the system may charge, and see what was charged.
It appears in online stores, subscription services, app stores, ride-share and food apps, browsers, operating-system wallets, and now in AI/Agent products that buy things for a person.
Before saved payment methods, a buyer typed a card number into every checkout. Saving the card once made repeat purchases fast, and moved the risk to whoever stores it.

Card networks answered that risk with the PCI DSS rules for anyone who stores card numbers, and later with network tokens: the merchant stores a token that only works for that merchant, while the real card number stays with the card network or wallet.

Wallets such as Apple Pay and Google Pay moved the stored card into the device or the platform account, so a merchant never sees the card number at all and the buyer approves each charge with a fingerprint, face or device passcode.
Who holds the card — the merchant, a payment processor, a wallet, or a password manager. The fewer parties that hold the real card number, the less there is to leak.
Who approves a charge — a saved card can be charged with no step from the buyer, or each charge can need an approval step, a biometric check, or a 3-D Secure challenge from the bank.
Limits — spending caps, single-use or merchant-locked virtual cards, and per-transaction approval bound what a stolen or misused method can cost.
Visibility and revocation — the buyer can see each charge and remove a method or a token without cancelling the card.

A typical flow: the buyer adds a method once; a processor such as Stripe stores it and returns a token; at checkout the system charges the token; the bank may ask the buyer to approve the charge; the system shows a receipt and keeps a history.
Subscription billing, the money a service charges its own user, uses the same parts. It differs from purchases the service makes from other merchants on the user's behalf.
An agent that pays for things needs a payment method it can use without seeing a card number it could leak or misuse.

As of November 2026 the approaches in use are a wallet the agent draws on, with a network token per merchant and the person's biometric approval on each purchase, as in ChatGPT/Wallet; a checkout the merchant and the AI vendor build together around a payment token scoped to one purchase, as in OpenAI's 2025 Instant Checkout; and a browser agent that reaches the merchant's checkout and pauses for the person to enter or approve the payment, as in ChatGPT/Cloud/Browser.
The same split appears in Credential/Manage/ment: the agent gets a scoped, short-lived grant, and the long-lived secret stays with the person or their wallet.
ChatGPT/Q/Does ChatGPT have any payment management? looks at what ChatGPT offers.
PayPal’s tools for merchants to accept payments initiated by shopping agents. PayPal can also appear as the shopper’s payment method when the checkout offers it.

What the shopper sees. PayPal describes a limited rollout of Pay with PayPal for eligible purchases in ChatGPT. When the option appears, the shopper signs in or confirms with a passkey and approves the purchase in PayPal. Which ChatGPT plans and retailers currently offer this checkout is unverified. PayPal’s AI shopping guide

What the merchant receives. In PayPal’s documented integration for ChatGPT apps, the shopper authorizes PayPal and the merchant’s app receives a delegated payment token. Braintree processes the payment using that token. This lets the checkout use the shopper’s approval without passing the shopper’s PayPal password to the agent. PayPal developer guide

How ChatGPT checkout changed. PayPal announced the OpenAI partnership in October 2025 around Instant Checkout. OpenAI shifted toward merchant-run checkouts in March 2026. A specific seller’s checkout determines whether a shopper can choose PayPal. PayPal partnership announcement · OpenAI shopping update

Where ChatGPT Wallet fits. ChatGPT/Wallet uses an eligible saved card for purchases approved in a conversation with a dot. A Pay with PayPal button opens PayPal’s own approval flow. Listed personal bills can be paid through PayPal/Bill Pay. ChatGPT Wallet guide · PayPal’s AI shopping guide

U.S. PayPal Personal accounts can use the app or website to pay a listed biller. The user links the bill using the account details from their statement, verifies the amount and due date, and submits the payment in PayPal. Eligible bills can also be scheduled. PayPal Bill Pay help

For a medical lab bill. Coverage depends on whether the biller appears in PayPal’s directory and accepts the account details on the statement. If the biller is listed, the user can pay through PayPal. PayPal says some payments take several days to appear in the biller’s system. PayPal Bill Pay help

What an agent can do. As of November 21, 2026, the documented workflow has the user submit payment in PayPal. An agent may help identify the amount and due date, but a supported integration that lets ChatGPT or Claude submit through PayPal Bill Pay is unverified. PayPal/Agent Ready documents merchant checkout for shopping, a separate workflow. PayPal Bill Pay help · PayPal Agent Ready overview
